summary.intent: Autonomously run the full GSD post-execute-phase ship loop for phase 67 (TEE republish lease-renewer rewrite): verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, ship as a PR, resolve all review threads, and extract learnings — without stopping for user input except on genuine ambiguity or the final merge decision.
summary.outcome: PR #585 was created and fully shipped: all gates (verify/secure/validate/SDK E2E) passed, over 30 CodeRabbit/Greptile findings across 3 review rounds were triaged (fixes applied and re-tested, deferrals filed as 4 todos), a CI-only SDK E2E failure was diagnosed and fixed, all 10 review threads were resolved, CI finished 26 pass/0 fail, and 67-LEARNINGS.md (31 items) was committed — final HEAD 3f80a8ef0, merge left to the user.

repo: The tee-republish SDK E2E suite (added in phase 67-08) has no CI guard and CI provisions neither a live TEE worker nor the `cipherbox` DB (only `cipherbox_test`, and `DB_DATABASE` isn't exported to the e2e step) — the suite is inherently local-stack-only and must be gated with something like `skipIf(CI)` on both the module-level `beforeAll` and the `describe` block.

The commit helper can report a false-negative `commit_failed`/hang (looks like a 1Password SSH-signing stall) while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying, matches prior known behavior.

TypeORM's `update(criteria, partial)` has type friction (`FindOptionsWhere` vs nullable fields like `keyEpoch: number | null`) when adding extra scoping fields to a criteria object that previously worked untyped/loosely — non-null assertions or a query-builder CAS form are the two ways out.

GSD's gsd-secure-phase / gsd-validate-phase skills have a short-circuit path (skip auditor spawn) when the existing register/tests already fully cover requirements at plan-authored, ASVS L1 — but only if `register_authored_at_plan_time: true`; still worth running targeted test suites even when skipping the auditor to confirm 'runs green' durably.
CodeRabbit CLI review findings on `.planning/ROADMAP.md`/`STATE.md` progress-bar drift are real signal — these docs can silently desync from their own frontmatter after phase completion.

code.finding: signIpnsRecord became dead code once the route switched to renewIpnsRecord; its orphaned JSDoc had been left above renewIpnsRecord — both removed as a simplify pass.
Needed skipIf(CI) gating on both beforeAll and describe (no live TEE worker/DB in CI); also had a queue resource leak (missing try/finally) flagged by CodeRabbit.

getDueEntries only filtered encryptedIpnsPrivateKey non-null, but code later dereferenced signedRecord!/keyEpoch! outside the try/catch — one null row could abort the whole batch; fixed with a stricter null-safety filter.

Epoch-upgrade write lacked tombstoned_at IS NULL guard and userId scope, risking a tombstoned record getting a re-encrypted key (violates tombstone-immutability guarantee) — fixed by scoping the update/CAS to tombstone+owner+epoch.
Missing same-sequence invariant check before publish (TEE-02 defense-in-depth against a misbehaving TEE) — added as a guard.
Re-enrollment only refreshed nextRepublishAt without reactivating a stale/inactive row, so it never rejoined the due-entries batch — fixed to reactivate on re-enroll.
TEE key validation/wrap block ran after the seal+IPFS upload; reordered before upload to fail closed and avoid orphaned blobs on invalid keys.
Added a fail-closed test asserting currentEpoch must be a positive integer, locking in the earlier NaN/negative-epoch guard fix.

workflow: When a background `beforeAll` guard (e.g., a migration-drop assertion) queries infra unconditionally, it can fail in environments (CI) that skip the tests it's guarding but still execute the setup hook — setup-hook side effects need their own environment gating, separate from the test-skip logic.
After any push to a PR, `git fetch` + rebase must run first if a release bot may have pushed a `chore(release)` commit in the interim — verified this repeatedly across the ship loop.
Waiting for background task notifications instead of polling in a loop kept the ship process from busy-waiting during multi-minute CodeRabbit/CI runs.

Re-running the full local test suite (targeted packages, not full monorepo) after each round of review fixes caught a transient startup-timing flake (BullMQ/tee_key_state race) distinguishable from a real regression by re-running once more.

friction: CI's SDK E2E job failed post-push because the newly added tee-republish suite required a live TEE worker + `cipherbox` DB that CI doesn't provision — required a diagnostic detour into the CI workflow config to find the root cause.
The commit helper reported a `commit_failed`/hang on the simplify-edits commit that had actually landed, requiring manual `git log` verification per known gotcha.

A background poll for CodeRabbit + Greptile reviews exited with code 1 after ~16 minutes due to a transient `api.github.com` network blip on the final query, requiring a re-query to confirm actual state.

Fixing the epoch-upgrade write (adding tombstone/userId scope) introduced a TypeScript FindOptionsWhere friction and broke an existing spec's mock expectations, requiring an extra fix-test-refix cycle.

A test re-run after the getDueEntries fix showed an 18.99s failure that turned out to be a flake (API had just restarted, BullMQ/tee_key_state race) rather than a real regression, requiring a second clean run to confirm.
An 'API Error: Internal server error' interrupted the assistant mid-step (updating the PR body before shipping), though work resumed cleanly afterward.
